display_name: Heltec Vision Master E290 (ESP32-S3 + 2.9" e-paper + SX1262)

mcu.flash_mb_provenance: measured - esp_flash_get_size() on silicon settled an 8 vs 16 MB documentation conflict in favour of the board definition (reference project A, docs/e290-hardware-reference.md)
mcu.psram_note: QSPI per the board definition, size unmeasured. A runtime reading of 0 bytes is EXPECTED, not a fault: BOARD_HAS_PSRAM is not defined by this board definition, so the core never initialises SPIRAM. To measure it, rebuild with -DBOARD_HAS_PSRAM.

fqbn_note: Use the vendor board definition from the stock esp32:esp32 core and change nothing. The intuitive manual guesses - OPI PSRAM and 16 MB flash - both contradict the board definition, and the flash guess is measured wrong. Prefer the stock core over the Heltec fork, which emits many warnings from its own vendored IDF headers.

strapping.0: BOOT button (S2) + strapping. Already committed on this board.
strapping.3: E-Ink CS + strapping. Already committed on this board.
strapping.45: LED_POWER + strapping (VDD_SPI select). Especially dangerous: an external pull-up switches flash to 1.8 V and bricks boot.
strapping.46: ADC_CTRL, the battery-divider enable, active HIGH + strapping. Must be LOW at boot, so never fit an external pull-up to GPIO46.

consumed.7: VBAT_READ (ADC1_CH6). On THIS board GPIO7 is battery sense - on the superseded CrowPanel 2.13 v1 the same number is the panel power-enable. Never carry a GPIO number between boards.
consumed.18: Vext - gates the e-ink 3V3 rail, active HIGH
consumed.46: ADC_CTRL battery-divider enable, active HIGH + strapping

conditional_free.21: USER button (S3). Shareable as a deep-sleep wake source if diode-OR'd with the button, which is the only RTC-capable pin left on this board.
conditional_free.38: QuickLink I2C SCL. Available for I2C peripherals on the QuickLink bus; not available as a general GPIO.
conditional_free.39: QuickLink I2C SDA. Available for I2C peripherals on the QuickLink bus; not available as a general GPIO.
conditional_free.43: UART0 TX. Free only with a USB-CDC console - the board JSON already sets ARDUINO_USB_CDC_ON_BOOT=1.
conditional_free.44: UART0 RX. Free only with a USB-CDC console. Note it is NOT RTC-capable, so it cannot be a wake source.

contradicted_header_pins.11: Heltec's own documentation tells you not to use header pin 11.

onboard_i2c.connector_provenance: schematic symbol reading - verify with a meter before crimping

rails.warning: Do not power a MAX98357A class-D amplifier from this LDO. It can pull ~1 A peak into 4 ohm. Run it from VBAT with its own bulk capacitance.

charge.source: R18 = 2 kOhm / 5%, schematic rev V0.3.1. R17 = 330 ohm is the LED resistor, not R_PROG.
charge.min_cell_note: Cell sizing FOLLOWS FROM the charge current. At ~600 mA a 1000 mAh cell charges at 0.6C, which is comfortable; a 500 mAh cell sees 1.2C, which is too high for most pouch cells. Not adjustable from firmware.
open_gates: Verify R18 on the physical board reads 2 kOhm.
Confirm the 1200/R_PROG constant against the LGS4056H datasheet.

battery_connector.warning: A JST-PH 2.0 mm cell lead does NOT mate with this socket. Polarity is not standardised - meter it before plugging anything in.

battery_sense.warning: State of charge is unreadable while on USB: the charger holds BAT at its ~4.2 V float voltage whether a cell is present or not. A reading of 4.201 V with no cell fitted is the expected result, not a calibration check.

sleep_current_ua.conflict: Datasheet section 1.2 text says 20 uA; Table 3.2 and the product page say 18 uA. No independent measurement was found.
sleep_current_ua.how_to_close: Meter in series with the battery positive lead, uA range, USB DISCONNECTED.

lora.note: The regional band variant is fixed when you order. You cannot change it later.

antenna_2g4.conflict: The spec table and Meshtastic say U.FL; Heltec's own product FAQ says a spring antenna with no connector. Inspect the physical board before designing a second antenna port.

display.active_offset_note: The active area sits 3.05 mm off the module centre along the long axis, toward the end away from the FPC. A symmetric margin clips 0.85 mm off the active area.

mechanical.header: 2x20 female on the underside of the long edge. Removing it takes the board+panel stack from 12.01 mm to ~2.8-3.0 mm.
mechanical.mounting_holes: Dimensioned by Heltec as SLOTS with no size given. A slot does not constrain position along its long axis, so locating posts are invalid.
mechanical.cad_models: None published. No STEP, no DXF - only PDFs and a pin-map PNG. CAD must be driven from dimensions.

pin_notes.7: VBAT_READ. Reading it requires GPIO46 (ADC_CTRL) driven HIGH first.
pin_notes.14: LoRa DIO1. Raiding GPIO8-14 for buttons is tempting because they are RTC-capable, but it forecloses LoRa.
pin_notes.17: The only free ADC pin, and it is ADC2_CH6 - unusable while Wi-Fi is active.
pin_notes.18: Vext. The e-ink rail is properly gated here; assert it HIGH and settle before talking to the panel.
pin_notes.21: USER button S3. The proposed deep-sleep wake pin, diode-OR'd with the button.
pin_notes.44: UART0 RX. NOT RTC-capable, so an expander interrupt cannot live here.

notes: There is NO free ADC1 channel. ADC1 is GPIO1-10 and every one is used. This rules out a resistor-ladder keypad and forces an I2C GPIO expander or an I2C ADC.
Only GPIO0-21 are RTC-capable, so GPIO38-48 cannot wake the chip from deep sleep via EXT0/EXT1.
All four strapping pins (0, 3, 45, 46) are already committed by the board.
Using GPIO40/41/42 costs hardware JTAG debugging. USB-Serial-JTAG on GPIO19/20 is unaffected.
Keep GPIO8-14 free of other uses if LoRa is wanted, even as a stretch goal.

Every GPIO assignment here was confirmed by at least three of: datasheet section 2.2, the schematic, espressif/arduino-esp32 variants/heltec_vision_master_e290/pins_arduino.h, and meshtastic/firmware variants/esp32s3/heltec_vision_master_e290/variant.h.
Heltec's docs page links the datasheet with a space in the filename, which 404s. Do not plan on fetching it at runtime.

sources.note: Boilerplate shared across Heltec's ESP32 range. Contradicts the schematic on the charge IC. Recorded so its claims can be identified, not counted.

gpio_map.note: Every GPIO assignment confirmed by at least three of these four. This was previously a prose note that nothing could check.

power.note: Charge path from the schematic; sleep current disputed between vendor documents.

contradictions.impact: Dominates the long tail of any battery-life estimate. power_budget.py reports a runtime RANGE rather than a point estimate because of this.
contradictions.how_to_close: Meter in series with the battery positive lead, uA range, USB DISCONNECTED.

contradictions.impact: Whether a second antenna port can be designed into an enclosure at all.

readings.note: Generic boilerplate shared across Heltec's whole ESP32 range

contradictions.resolved_by: The schematic names the part actually fitted; the FAQ page is boilerplate that is identical across unrelated Heltec products, so it is not a source about this board.
contradictions.impact: Sets the charge-current formula and therefore the minimum safe cell capacity.

contradictions.resolved_by: esp_flash_get_size() on the physical board. Silicon beats both documents.
contradictions.impact: Partition layout. Believing 16 MB would silently truncate an OTA partition.

open_questions.question: Verify R18 on the physical board reads 2 kOhm.
open_questions.impact: Confirms the charge current, which is a battery-safety number currently resting on a schematic reading.

open_questions.question: Confirm the 1200/R_PROG charge constant against the LGS4056H datasheet.
